name.text: Reflection and symmetry in a building facade (interactive)

questiontext.text:
An architect is finishing a scale drawing of a building on a metre grid. {@intro@} The red dashed line is the line of symmetry.

{@task@}

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ans1="rW" input-ref-ans2="rD" width="480px" height="480px"]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: {#bbox#}, keepaspectratio: true, axis: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}, defaultAxes: { x: { ticks: { insertTicks: false, ticksDistance: 1, minorTicks: 0, drawLabels: true } }, y: { ticks: { insertTicks: false, ticksDistance: 1, minorTicks: 0, drawLabels: true } } } }); var cH = {#cH#}; // 1 = lake (reflect in y=0), 0 = facade (reflect in x=0) var WL = {#WL#}, DL = {#DL#}, TL = {#TL#}; var SH = {#shellL#}; var parkW = {#parkW#}, parkD = {#parkD#}; function mir(p) { return cH ? [p[0], -p[1]] : [-p[0], p[1]]; } // a point whose position is (getC()[0]+dx, getC()[1]+dy), updating live function fpt(getC, dx, dy) { return board.create('point', [function () { return getC()[0] + dx; }, function () { return getC()[1] + dy; }], {visible: false, fixed: true}); } function poly(P, col, op, dash) { board.create('polygon', P, { fillColor: col, fillOpacity: op, borders: {strokeColor: col, strokeWidth: 2, dash: dash}, vertices: {visible: false}, fixed: true, highlight: false, hasInnerPoints: false }); } function shell(pts, given) { var P = pts.map(function (q) { return board.create('point', q, {visible: false, fixed: true}); }); poly(P, given ? '#e7e2d6' : '#dced', given ? 0.6 : 0.45, given ? 0 : 2); } function tri(pts, col) { var P = pts.map(function (q) { return board.create('point', q, {visible: false, fixed: true}); }); poly(P, col, 0.55, 0); } function windowAt(getC, col) { var h = 1; poly([fpt(getC, -h, -h), fpt(getC, h, -h), fpt(getC, h, h), fpt(getC, -h, h)], col, 0.2, 0); board.create('segment', [fpt(getC, 0, -h), fpt(getC, 0, h)], {strokeColor: col, strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}); board.create('segment', [fpt(getC, -h, 0), fpt(getC, h, 0)], {strokeColor: col, strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } function doorAt(getC, col) { // 1.4 m wide, 2.6 m tall, centred on getC var hw = 0.5, hh = 1; poly([fpt(getC, -hw, -hh), fpt(getC, hw, -hh), fpt(getC, hw, hh), fpt(getC, -hw, hh)], col, 0.3, 0); board.create('point', [function () { return getC()[0]; }, function () { return getC()[1]; }], {name: '', size: 1, fixed: true, fillColor: col, strokeColor: col, highlight: false}); } // mirror line / horizon if (cH) { board.create('line', [[-9, 0], [9, 0]], {strokeColor: '#c00', dash: 2, straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, fixed: true, highlight: false}); board.create('text', [5.4, 0.4, 'water (y = 0)'], {fontSize: 12, color: '#c00', fixed: true}); } else { board.create('line', [[0, -9], [0, 9]], {strokeColor: '#c00', dash: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); board.create('text', [0.3, 7.4, 'x = 0'], {fontSize: 12, color: '#c00', fixed: true}); } // building shell: given half + mirrored (decorative) half shell(SH, true); shell(SH.map(mir), false); // given (original) features windowAt(function () { return WL; }, '#1e6fd0'); doorAt(function () { return DL; }, '#8a5a2b'); // triangular pediment above the door: original + reflected (both drawn) - the congruence subject tri(TL, '#e08a00'); tri(TL.map(mir), '#e08a00'); // draggable markers for the reflected window and door var pW = board.create('point', parkW, {name: 'Window', size: 4, fillColor: '#1e6fd0', strokeColor: '#12508f', snapToGrid: true, snapSizeX: 0.5, snapSizeY: 0.5, label: {offset: [8, 8], fontSize: 13}}); The architect added a triangular pediment (the orange triangle) above the door, and mirrored it onto the reflected side. Is the reflected pediment congruent to the original one?

[[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

The reflection rule. {@rulewords@} So each feature keeps one coordinate and has the other negated:

  • Window: original {@WL@} \(\to\) reflection {@ta1@}
  • Door: original {@DL@} \(\to\) reflection {@ta2@}

A mirror image sits the same perpendicular distance from the line of symmetry as the original, but on the opposite side.

Congruence. A reflection is a rigid motion (an isometry): it preserves every length and angle. The reflected pediment is therefore congruent to the original — the same size and shape, just mirror-reversed (its orientation is flipped). It is not merely similar, and reflection never changes size.

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

node.description: Left on the same side as the original?

truefeedback.text: The window marker is still on the same side as the original — it hasn't crossed the line of symmetry. A mirror image must be the same distance from the line, but on the opposite side.
You reflected in the wrong direction. The line of symmetry here is the {@mirrorword@}, so the marker should flip across that line, not the other one.

falsefeedback.text: The window isn't in the symmetric position yet. It must be the same perpendicular distance from the line of symmetry as the original window, on the opposite side.

truefeedback.text: The door marker is still on the same side as the original — it hasn't crossed the line of symmetry. A mirror image must be the same distance from the line, but on the opposite side.
You reflected in the wrong direction. The line of symmetry here is the {@mirrorword@}, so the marker should flip across that line, not the other one.

falsefeedback.text: The door isn't in the symmetric position yet. It must be the same perpendicular distance from the line of symmetry as the original door, on the opposite side.

truefeedback.text: Similar means "same shape". These are more than that: a reflection preserves every length and angle, so the two triangles are exactly the same size — they are congruent.
A reflection is a rigid motion — it flips the shape over the line but never stretches or shrinks it. The mirror image is the same size, so it is congruent.
